body:
> Split out of #129 after the 2026-08-28 spike (job `cadca6f1`, Claude Code 2.1.251). Prerequisite for #129 piece B.

## What the spike showed

A track root that fans a wave out to subagents **ends its own turn while the children run**: the Agent tool ran in the background, the root parked itself with ScheduleWakeup, and `Stop` fired for the root *before* `SubagentStop` fired for the child. Measured order in the hook log:

```
23:22:45  PreToolUse  Agent                     (root, cwd kb-spike-129)
23:22:48  PreToolUse  Bash   agent_id=aff2ce…    (child, cwd .claude/worktrees/agent-aff2ce…)
23:22:54  Stop                                  (root — children still running)
23:23:03  SubagentStop      agent_id=aff2ce…
23:23:19  PreToolUse  Write                     (root resumes)
```

`stopHook` (`src/hook.js`) answers that moment with what it does for every idle worker: the root's task is still `running` on the board, so it writes `{decision: "block"}` with the terminal-verb nudge — twice per attempt (`.kanban/nudges/<n>-<k>`), then allows. On an orchestrator that is *correctly* waiting for its wave, that is two false nudges per wave, each one pushing the root to file a verb on a root whose children are not done — exactly the protocol violation the hook exists to prevent.

## What

Teach the Stop hook to tell "idle because the work is done" from "idle because the work is running in subagents".

- The Stop payload carries `session_id`, `cwd`, `stop_hook_active` and (for subagent ends) `agent_id`; the root's `SubagentStop` firings carry `agent_id` too. Record live subagents from the hook side — `SubagentStop` is the only "ended" signal a hook sees, and the `PreToolUse` for `Agent` is the "started" one — under `.kanban/sessions/` beside the existing markers, so a Stop on a session with **started > ended** subagents returns 0 with a one-line stderr note instead of a nudge. Pure decision in `src/model.js` (`shouldNudgeOnStop(state)`), tested with the hook log above as a fixture.
- A root whose subagents have all ended and whose task is still `running` is nudged as today — that is the real "you forgot the verb" case.
- The nudge counter does not burn on a suppressed Stop: the two real nudges are still available once the wave is finished.
- The `PreToolUse` hook already runs for `Agent` (matcher `*`); register `SubagentStop` in the same settings block `hkb init` writes (`src/init.js`) and in `hooks/hooks.json` for the plugin, both the local and `--shared-hooks` forms.
- Cold workers (no `Agent` on their allowlist) never start a subagent, so nothing changes for them.

## Constraints

- No new API call in the hook: everything it needs is on stdin and under `.kanban/`.
- Never suppress on a guess: if the marker directory cannot be read, nudge as today — a false nudge costs a turn, a missed one costs the protocol.
- The `KB_TASK`/worktree-name gate stays exactly as it is (`whichAttempt`); this changes only what the hook says, not whom it applies to.

## Done when

- A Stop fired while a subagent is live returns 0, logs why, and leaves the nudge counter untouched (fixture from the spike log).
- A Stop fired after every subagent ended on a still-running task nudges exactly as today.
- `hkb init` and the plugin register `SubagentStop`; `hkb doctor` reports its absence on an older board the way it reports a missing Stop hook.
- `node --test test/model.test.js test/skill.test.js test/init.test.js` cover the three cases; `npm run lint && npm test` green.
title: The Stop hook must not nudge a track root whose subagents are still running
